standard-dialogue-first-time-speaking-to.npc: Getting ready to go fishing of course. There's no time to waste!
I've got all the supplies I need from the shop at the end of the pier. They sell good rope, hammers and axes although their bailing buckets aren't too effective.

steps.npc: I get all sorts, anything that lies on the sea bed, you never know what you're going to get until you pull up the net!

options.text: Your boat doesn't look too safe.

steps.player: Your boat doesn't look too safe.

steps.npc: That's because it's not, the darn thing's full of holes.

steps.player: Oh, so I suppose you can't go out for a while?

steps.npc: Oh no, I don't let a few holes stop an experienced sailor like me. I could sail these seas in a barrel, I'll be going out soon enough.
Well of course you can! I'll warn you though, the seas are merciless and without fishing experience you won't catch much.
You need a fishing level of 15 or above to catch any fish on the trawler.
On occasions the net rips, so you'll need some rope to repair it.
Repairing the net is difficult in the harsh conditions so you'll find it easier with a higher crafting level.
There's also a slight problem with leaks.
Nothing some swamp paste won't fix...
Also, there's the small matter of the Kraken.

steps.player: You have got to be kidding me?

steps.npc: Occupational hazard. I usually whack it with an axe a few time and fix the damage with hammer once it's gone.
Oh, and one more thing... I hope you're a good swimmer?

options.text: Actually, I think I'll leave it.

steps.player: Actually, I think I'll leave it.

steps.npc: Bloomin' land lovers!!!

steps.text: If the trawler is in port:

steps.npc: Aye aye! Meet me on board the trawler. I just need to get a few things together.

steps.text: If the trawler is at sea:

steps.npc: Aye aye! Meet me on board the trawler.
Oh hang on. I'm already on a fishing trip with someone. You'll have to try back in a few minutes.

steps.player: How can you be here and on board the boat?!

steps.npc: That's Game Magic, [lass/son].
Never mind. Just try back later OK?
Swamp tar mixed with flour which is then heated over a fire.

steps.player: Where can I find swamp tar?

steps.npc: Unfortunately the only supply of swamp tar is in the swamps below Lumbridge.

standard-dialogue-subsequent-conversatio.text: If does not have a sextant:

steps.text: Murphy has given you a sextant.
a sextant

standard-dialogue-subsequent-conversatio.text: If the player has a sextant:

steps.npc: Good day to you land lover. Fancy hitting the high seas again?

options.text: No thanks, I still feel ill from last time.

steps.player: No thanks, I still feel ill from last time.

steps.npc: Hah! ...Softy.

options.text: We keep sinking! Can you give me some advice?

steps.player: We keep sinking! Can you give me some advice?

steps.npc: Aye aye matey! We'll soon get you ship shape!
You need a fishing level of 15 or above to catch any fish on the trawler.
On occasions the net rips, so you'll need some rope to repair it.
Repairing the net is difficult in the harsh conditions so you'll find it easier with a higher crafting level.
There's also a slight problem with leaks.
Nothing some swamp paste won't fix...
Also, bring a good axe and a hammer in case of Kraken attacks.

steps.player: I thought I'd heard it all!
Right so I need lots of swamp paste and plenty of rope, an axe and a hammer. Thanks Murphy!

steps.npc: If all else fails use a bailing bucket or three!

options.text: Could you teach me to how to trawl for myself?

steps.text: Player owns a boat:

steps.npc: I'm afraid my setup is a bit dated these days. That said, I've heard there's a retired netmaster over in Port Roberts who's more than happy to share his trawling secrets. Kellan I think his name was.

steps.text: Player has talked to Netmaster Kellan:

steps.player: Ah yes, I think I've met him. I'll have to go and have another word with him about it.

steps.text: Player has not talked to Kellan:

steps.player: Interesting... I might have to sail over there and introduce myself.

steps.text: Player does not own a boat:

steps.npc: You won't be able to trawl without a boat of your own. Perhaps someone over at Port Sarim could help you with that.
Ahoy there! All set for a dive?

steps.text: If the player does not have a fishbowl helmet:

steps.player: Murphy, can I get another diving helmet?

steps.npc: Sure, here you go. Try not to lose this one, I'm not a very good glassblower.

steps.text: a fishbowl helmet

steps.npc: Well, the bowls I make tend to shatter under pressure into razor-sharp shards of lethal, face shredding shrapnel.
Don't let it bother you, I think I know what I'm doing wrong now.

steps.text: If the player does not have a diving apparatus:

steps.player: Hello Murphy. Do you have a spare diving backpack?

steps.npc: Sure, I have plenty after the...little incident.
Nothing to worry yourself about.
Here, have this one. Only dropped once!

steps.text: a diving apparatus

steps.npc: No, no.
Well, yes.
But seriously, what are the chances of getting a jellyfish jammed in there again?

steps.text: If the player has a weapon or shield equipped:

steps.npc: Well let's be...
Err, how do you plan on swimming with your hands full?
Well, when you hit the water you will start swimming. If you can't free up your hands by putting everything away then you will sink like a stone.
All you have to do is have 2 spaces to store the items and you are good to go.
Even if you aren't carrying a shield or weapon it's always handy to have some free space for an emergency.
See you then!

steps.text: If the player has a gnomeball in their inventory:

steps.npc: Now, do you have a gomeball on you?

steps.player: Yes, I do, why do you ask?

steps.npc: Well you will need to leave them on the surface. They are so full of air that they will stop you diving properly.

steps.player: Right, I'll go put it in the bank.

steps.text: If the player has an handegg in their inventory:

steps.npc: Now, do you have a hand egg on you?

steps.player: Yes, I do, why do you ask?

steps.npc: Well you will need to leave them on the surface. They are so full of air that they will stop you diving properly.

steps.player: Right, I'll go put it in the bank.

steps.text: If the player has a cat following them:

steps.npc: You want that cat of yours to drown or something?

steps.player: You mean you can't make them an adorable set of tiny diving gear?

steps.npc: No. Just...no.
I'm not taking you out for a dive with that cat following you.
I'm not a cat person, and it'd have to stay on the ship while you were down.

steps.text: If the player has a cat in their inventory:

steps.npc: You know, I can see your cat right there.
I'm looking right at it. See, it's just there in your bag!
I'm not taking you out with that cat. I'm not some sort of cat-sitter, so go and put it somewhere safe, then come back.

steps.player: I still think I should get some cat-sized diving gear...

steps.text: If the player is followed by a different pet:

steps.npc: I'm not taking you out for a dive with that pet following you. It'll get wet.

steps.text: If the player has a pet in their inventory:

steps.npc: I'm not taking you out for a dive with that pet in your bag. It'll get wet.

steps.text: If the player does not have a fishbowl helmet and diving apparatus equipped:

steps.npc: Well I can't take you out until you are properly geared up.
We lost three diving parties that way!

steps.player: Ok, well I'll just put my diving helmet and diving backpack on.

steps.text: If the player is carrying 27kg of equipment or more:

steps.npc: Well that's the sort of spirit I like to see. However you are far too heavy to go diving right now.
Well, I can't take you diving if you are carrying more than 27kg worth of equipment.
We arrived at that number through trial and error, and the errors were not pretty let me assure you.
Well, if you pop over to a bank and leave all your heavy equipment behind then I'll take you out.
See you then!

steps.text: If none of the previous conditions apply:

steps.npc: Ok, let's be off then.

steps.text: A brief cutscene plays of Murphy and the player standing on the trawler's deck at sea.

steps.npc: Good luck, I'll weigh anchor. Climb up the chain to get aboard.

steps.text: The player dives down to the Mogre Camp.

steps.npc: Ok, well I'll be here if you change your mind.

standard-dialogue-when-climbing-back-up-.npc: Great, I'll take us back in.

standard-dialogue-when-climbing-back-up-.text: The player is transported back to Port Khazard.

standard-dialogue-when-on-the-trawler-s-.text: If the trawler is in port:

steps.npc: The ship's ready to depart.

steps.text: If this is the first time speaking to Murphy on deck:

steps.npc: By the way, would you like me to remind you how the trawler works once the trip starts?

steps.text: If the player has talked to Murphy on deck before:

steps.npc: By the way, would you like me to keep reminding you how the trawler works once the trip starts?
You've got it!
No worries! Let me know if you change your mind!

standard-dialogue-when-on-the-trawler-s-.text: If a trawler is currently at sea:

steps.npc: The ship's at sea at the moment. This is some kind of paradox.

options.text: I've had enough, take me back.

steps.player: I've had enough, take me back.

steps.npc: Hah! .. the soft land lovers lost their sea legs have they?
We're too far out now, It'd be dangerous.

options.text: I insist Murphy, take me back.

steps.player: I insist Murphy, take me back.

steps.npc: Ok, ok, I'll try, but don't say I didn't warn you...

steps.text: Murphy attempts to sharply turn the large ship.

steps.npc: Save yourself! We're going down!

steps.text: The fishing trawler is wrecked at sea.

options.text: Okay then Murphy, just keep us afloat.

steps.player: Okay then Murphy, just keep us afloat.

steps.npc: That's the attitude sailor...Aaaaar!
Get those fishies!
I think i'm feeling a bit sea sick!
It's a fierce sea today traveller, you best hold on tight.

standard-dialogue-first-time-obtaining-t.player: I'm trying to learn how to be a navigator.

standard-dialogue-first-time-obtaining-t.npc: Well, you've come to the right place, m'hearty! What do you need to know?

standard-dialogue-first-time-obtaining-t.player: The professor said that I need to have a sextant. Do you know where I can get one?

standard-dialogue-first-time-obtaining-t.npc: Hmm. I used to use a sextant when I was a young fella.

standard-dialogue-first-time-obtaining-t.text: Murphy has given you his old sextant.

standard-dialogue-first-time-obtaining-t.npc: I can tell from the taste of the sea spray where I am, m'hearty!

via-astral-contact.player: Don't worry, Murphy. My name's [player name] and I'm using magic to contact you!

via-astral-contact.text: If the player is near Murphy:

steps.npc: That's so rude when you may as well just speak to me in person!
Well I never! Technology these days. Beyond me. So how might I help you?

steps.player: I was just wondering if there is anyone down there helping you out on the trawler?

steps.text: If a fishing trawler trip is currently underway:

steps.npc: The boat has just left actually! Perhaps when it comes back you can join them in another run?

steps.text: If people are waiting for the next trawler to depart:

steps.npc: There seems to be someone on-board.

steps.text: If it is just one person:

steps.npc: Yep, just one.

steps.text: If there are more people waiting:

steps.npc: No, there are [number] at the moment.

steps.text: If there are no people waiting or at sea:

steps.npc: The boat is just sitting waiting for someone to join. How about it?

steps.player: Maybe I'll come have a look. I'll catch you later!

steps.npc: Ok mate, bye!

overhead-dialogue-when-at-port.text: When waiting for the trawler to depart:

steps.npc: The ship is back in port!
The ship will leave in 1 minute!
The ship will leave in [50/40/30/20/10] seconds!

overhead-dialogue-when-at-port.text: When the trawler is out at sea:

steps.npc: The ship has just left port!
The ship will be back in [5/4/3/2/1] minute[s]!
The ship will be back in under 1 minute!

overhead-dialogue-when-at-port.text: When crossing the gangplank back on the docks as the only person waiting on board:

steps.npc: Looks like the ship's not going after all!

overhead-dialogue-when-at-port.text: When the trawler is wrecked at sea:

steps.npc: The ship has sunk! I'll get another one.

overhead-dialogue-when-on-deck.text: While waiting for the trawler to depart:

steps.npc: The ship will leave in 1 minute!
The ship will leave in [50/40/30/20/10] seconds!

overhead-dialogue-when-at-sea.text: When first arriving at open sea:

steps.npc: Let's get this net full with fishies!

overhead-dialogue-when-at-sea.text: When the net has been torn:

steps.npc: Arrh! Check that net!

overhead-dialogue-when-at-sea.text: When under assault of the Kraken:

steps.npc: Doom! The Kraken is attacking!

overhead-dialogue-when-at-sea.text: When the Kraken has been fought back:

steps.npc: Hurrah! The Kraken is no more!

overhead-dialogue-when-at-sea.text: When the lower deck is about to become water-filled:

steps.npc: You'll need to start bailing soon!
Blistering barnacles!
The water is coming in matey!

overhead-dialogue-when-at-sea.text: When the lower deck is water-filled:

steps.npc: We'll all end up in a watery grave!
Land lubbers!
It's a fierce sea today traveller.
My mother could bail better than that!

overhead-dialogue-when-at-sea.text: When the trawler is about to sink:

steps.npc: Noooooo!
We're going under!
We're all doomed!
Mummy!
You'll need all your strength!
To make it back to shore.
No fishies for you today!
Arrrgh! We've sunk!
Keep your head above water shipmate.
You'll be joining Davey Jones!
